initiative.title: Research threads: multi-scale canvas for tasks and findings
initiative.summary: Unify tasks, findings, and questions into per-project threads with pedigree, a visible frontier, and recursive summary-over-detail at every scale.
initiative.next_action: Next slice: in-app summary drafting (callLLM) + manual card capture on the canvas

Notes - Updates: pyramids at all scales
ChatGPT connectors need OAuth or no-auth; DCR

claims.statement: Projects are research threads: tasks yield findings, which yield more tasks/questions; state is a frontier
Every layer has a summary plus details, recursively, at every scale (section, doc, thread, library)
Pedigree: each item has one primary parent (came-from) plus optional relates-to cross-links
Not everything must be in the main system; link external systems and capture only worthwhile parts (images, snippets)
Growth must be condensed; time, uniqueness, specificity decide visibility; delete vs hide undecided
Existing Tasks, Explorer, and Canvas each fall short; desire is one canvas across scales
Anchor use cases: learning a topic (collect, summarize, map next-to-learn frontier) first; decision/buying research (options stored but not overwhelming) next; all project types are real
Summaries: AI drafts on change, user accepts/edits; accepted text stable until refreshed
Clean slate: build threads with their own items; do not constrain on existing Tasks/Explorer/Canvas
Primary surface is a zoomable canvas
Writers: user plus agents via MCP (preferred, enables ChatGPT) or API; batch ingest of a whole exploration tree
Two hierarchies: pedigree edges (came-from) are separate from summary groupings that can span branches; zoom folds by summary group
Layout is computed from structure with manual nudges remembered
Agents write directly (add, link, close); every agent change is attributed and undoable as a batch
Finished/abandoned branches fold under summaries and fade; never auto-delete; manual deletion rare
One canvas per topic/project, many topics; each canvas self-contained, never one massive canvas
Items are cards that start short and can grow into a full rich note
Batch ingest sources: agent exploration trees, research reports (split into findings/sources/questions), own notes/dictation, web captures
Open tasks/questions stay visible when their group folds; revisit if cluttered
Card types: task, question, finding, source, summary, plus option and criterion for decisions
Library layer is a topic index (top summary, open count, last activity); no cross-topic links yet
Frontier generation comes from external agents only for now; no in-app agentic generation
Summaries are drafted in-app (context-bound, easy task); generation stays external
First usable version: agent posts exploration tree via MCP, renders on topic canvas with pedigree, fold-by-summary zoom, open items visible

shape.appetite: One vertical slice: topic model, ingest_tree service, MCP adapter, read-mostly canvas with semantic zoom. No in-app AI or manual-edit polish.
shape.problem: Agent-driven research produces a growing tree of tasks/findings that becomes overwhelming without pedigree, frontier visibility, and summary folding.
shape.recommended_shape: Per-topic canvas over a clean card model (7 types, came-from parent + relates-to links, summary groups as separate layer). ingest_tree is the core transactional, idempotent write; MCP is a thin adapter. Auto tree layout with nudges; semantic zoom folds accepted summary groups while open items stay visible.

first_proof.question: Does a zoomed-out topic canvas of agent-ingested work read as summaries plus a clear frontier?
first_proof.artifact: Real learning topic, 2-3 Claude Code ingest_tree rounds, 40-80 cards with summary drafts
first_proof.decision_rule: Readable and you would hand off the next question -> add in-app summaries + manual capture; frontier clutter -> revise fold rule first; layout fights groups -> revisit layout before more features
first_proof.result: Readable. Claude Code (sonnet) over local /mcp wrote 49 cards (20+14+18) incl. a full options x criteria decision and 3 draft summaries. After accepting, the canvas opens at Summaries (58%) showing 3 summary cards, the root question, and 8 open questions. Proof-driven fixes: fold descendants (stop at other summaries / below open cards), level-aware fit, readable state-batch names.
first_proof.decision: Pass: proceed to in-app summary drafting and manual capture next.
